official.title: PhD Position Indoor Thermal Natural Variation for Heat Resilience
official.description_text:
How do residents experience changing indoor temperatures? As a PhD candidate at TU Delft, you will combine citizen science, field data and modelling to help develop healthier and more energy-efficien.
Job description
Hot weather events are increasing, making adaptation of existing dwellings increasingly important to protect residents from unhealthy indoor conditions and limit future energy use for cooling. While we are instinctively drawn to natural conditions, residents are most of the time exposed to static environmental indoor conditions. Hot weather events can even amplify static conditions, for example through constant mechanical cooling. To support health and to lower energy use, current guidelines and standards allow for some variation. Yet we still know too little about how residents perceive and accept natural variation in indoor thermal conditions, and how this relates to building characteristics and resident behaviour.
As a PhD candidate at TU Delft, you will conduct research within the NWO-funded Nature 4 Homes project. Your research will address how natural variation in thermal conditions influences residents’ perceptions, acceptance and interactions with the building envelope under current and future Dutch conditions. This a unique opportunity to contribute to one of the most pressing challenges facing cities today: adapting existing dwellings to climate change while enhancing quality of life.
Using a citizen science approach, you will investigate indoor and outdoor thermal and ventilation conditions in existing dwellings in different regions of the Netherlands. You will combine measurements of environmental conditions with information about residents’ perceptions and behaviour and relevant building characteristics. A key part of your research will be developing new methods to characterize natural variation of indoor conditions in relation to outdoor conditions, and predicting this variation using climate scenarios and data collected in dwellings, in co-creation with residents, housing corporations and industy partners.
You will join the Architectural Engineering + Technology (AE&T) Department at the Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment, TU Delft, under the supervision of AnneMarie Eijkelenboom and Philomena M. Bluyssen and Gert-Jan Steeneveld of the Meteorology and Air Quality Section at Wageningen University and Research. You will collaborate closely with a postdoctoral researcher and three other PhD candidates, as well as research, industry and public-sector partners. We foster an open and collaborative environment, where independent thinking, knowledge sharing and interdisciplinary research are encouraged.
Job requirements
You hold an MSc in architecture, architectural engineering, meteorology or atmospheric sciences, environmental sciences, or civil engineering.
You have a strong interest in human perception, building design, and climate change.
You are motivated to conduct research with residents in real-world dwellings in the Netherlands.
You have affinity with modelling and analysing indoor and outdoor environmental conditions.
You enjoy interdisciplinary research and collaborating with academic, industry and public-sector partners.
You have excellent oral and written communication skills in English. For more details, please check the Graduate Schools Admission Requirements.
You have a fascination for science, and love working in an interdisciplinary team.
TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow.
These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.
At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional.
Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.
Challenge. Change. Impact!
Faculty Architecture & the Built Environment
The Faculty of Architecture and the Built Environment has a leading role in education and research worldwide. The driving force behind the faculty’s success is its robust research profile combined with the energy and creativity of its student body and academic community. It is buzzing with energy, with four thousand people enthusiastically studying, working, designing, conducting research and acquiring and disseminating knowledge. Our faculty has a strong focus on 'design-oriented research’, which has given it a top position in world rankings.
Staff and students are working to improve the built environment with the help of a broad set of disciplines, including architectural design, urban planning, building technology, social sciences, process management, and geo-information science. The faculty works closely with other faculties, universities, private parties, and the public sector, and has an extensive network in the Netherlands as well as internationally.

Conditions of employment
Doctoral candidates will be offered a 4-year period of employment in principle, but in the form of 2 employment contracts. An initial 1,5 year contract with an official go/no go progress assessment within 15 months. Followed by an additional contract for the remaining 2,5 years assuming everything goes well and performance requirements are met.
Salary and benefits are in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities, increasing from €3204 - €4051 gross per month, from the first year to the fourth year based on a fulltime contract (38 hours), plus 8% holiday allowance and an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.
As a PhD candidate you will be enrolled in the TU Delft Graduate School. The TU Delft Graduate School provides an inspiring research environment with an excellent team of supervisors, academic staff and a mentor. The Doctoral Education Programme is aimed at developing your transferable, discipline-related and research skills.
The TU Delft offers a customisable compensation package, discounts on health insurance, and a monthly work costs contribution. Flexible work schedules can be arranged.
Will you need to relocate to the Netherlands for this job? TU Delft is committed to make your move as smooth as possible! The HR unit,
Coming to Delft Service
, offers information on their website to help you prepare your relocation. In addition, Coming to Delft Service organises events to help you settle in the Netherlands, and expand your (social) network in Delft. A
Dual Career Programme
is available, to support your accompanying partner with their job search in the Netherlands.
Additional information
For more information about the application procedure, please contact paulien Stastra, HR Advisor,
e-mail:
recruitment-bk@tudelft.nl
.
The start date of this position is on March 1st 2027.
Application procedure
Please apply no later than
November 11, 2026
(local Dutch time + 2 hrs) via the application button and upload the following five items:
Your CV - highlighting examples of projects and/or achievements that demonstrate skills relevant to the advertised position.
Your motivation letter (no more than 600 words) addressing your interests and describing how your experience and plans fit with the position.
Copies of your BSc and MSc degrees and transcipts.
Names and contact information of at least three relevant references (letters not required at this stage).
Doing a PhD at TU Delft requires English proficiency at a certain level to ensure that the candidate is able to communicate and interact well, participate in English-taught Doctoral Education courses, and write scientific articles and a final thesis. For more details please check the
Graduate Schools Admission Requirements
.
Please note:
You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post.
As part of knowledge security, TU Delft conducts a risk assessment during the recruitment of personnel. We do this, among other things, to prevent the unwanted transfer of sensitive knowledge and technology. The assessment is based on information provided by the candidates themselves, such as their motivation letter and CV, and takes place at the final stages of the selection process. When the outcome of the assessment is negative, the candidate will be informed. The processing of personal data in the context of the risk assessment is carried out on the legal basis of the GDPR: performing a public task in the public interest. You can find more information about this assessment on our website about
knowledge security.
Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

ai.summary: Doctoral researcher position in built environment and thermal comfort at TU Delft (Architectural Engineering + Technology), investigating how residents perceive and accept natural variation in indoor thermal conditions under current and future Dutch climate scenarios. Research combines citizen science, field measurement, and modelling with co-creation involving residents and housing partners.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position focuses on human perception, behaviour, and acceptance—core HCI themes. Research involves residents as active participants in understanding environmental experience, which aligns with human-centred design principles. However, domain is climate adaptation and building physics rather than immersive learning, spatial cognition, or XR. Thematic distance is significant but methodology is shared.

methodological_fit.rationale: Strong methodological overlap: citizen science approach mirrors user-centred co-design; combining environmental measurements with resident perception/behaviour parallels mixed-methods HCI evaluation; interdisciplinary collaboration (meteorology, building physics, social sciences) matches researcher's cross-disciplinary experience. User studies and qualitative methods align with researcher's experimental-design and user-study skills. Modelling and prediction share quantitative research approaches.

growth_value.rationale: Position develops methodological skills directly applicable to immersive systems research: citizen science, co-creation with stakeholders, mixed-methods evaluation combining objective measurement and subjective perception, real-world deployment and longitudinal user engagement. Statistical analysis of environmental and behavioural data would strengthen quantitative research capability. Limited advancement in spatial cognition or immersive technology, but substantial growth in user-centred methodology and long-term engagement research.

strategic_value.rationale: TU Delft (priority-1 institution), Netherlands (preferred geography), 4-year funding, strong Faculty of Architecture with design-oriented research focus. Supervisors (AnneMarie Eijkelenboom, Philomena M. Bluyssen) have established HCI-adjacent research in built environment perception. NWO funding is nationally prestigious. Collaboration with Wageningen University expands network. However, built environment/climate adaptation is not core HCI/XR domain; publication venues and peer community would be architecture/engineering-focused, not HCI.

eligibility_flags: MSc in architecture, architectural engineering, meteorology/atmospheric sciences, environmental sciences, or civil engineering required; researcher's MSc in Creative Multimedia is adjacent but may not satisfy stated requirement—confirm with supervisors AnneMarie Eijkelenboom or Philomena M. Bluyssen before investing effort
Start date March 1, 2027; timing aligns with thesis completion if submitted by end of 2026
risks: Degree requirement mismatch (Creative Multimedia vs. architecture/engineering) may cause rejection despite methodological fit; clarification essential before application
Disciplinary focus is built environment and climate adaptation, not immersive systems or spatial cognition—knowledge transfer back to target domain would require active effort
Publication and peer communities are primarily architecture/engineering rather than HCI; may limit visibility within target field
No XR/immersive technology component; if goal is to develop human-centred XR expertise, this position develops adjacent but not directly applicable domain knowledge

eligibility_reasons: whether a completed degree is required before employment is not stated; your MSc is still in progress — verify with the source
